source_title: Marco Simoncelli’s parents pay emotional tribute 15 years after his death
source_excerpt: Fifteen years have passed since Marco Simoncelli lost his life in a tragic MotoGP accident. His family still feels his absence. They continue to live with the pain and grief, while memories of the Italian rider remain alive in the hearts of his family, friends and fans. His parents, Paolo and Rossella Simoncelli, paid an emotional tribute to their son ahead of the 2026 Malaysian Grand Prix.Marco Simoncelli's parents remember him ahead of Malaysian Grand PrixMarco Simoncelliâs parents, Paolo and Rossellaâs message brought back memories of a rider whose life ended far too soon at the Sepang International Circuit. The tribute was shared on social media along with pictures of the plaque placed at the corner where Simoncelli suffered his fatal crash."Some places hold memories that will never fade. Always with us, Marco," they wrote.ID@undefined Caption not available.The Sepang circuit has a special but painful connection with the Simoncelli family. It was here that the Italian suffered the accident that took his life on October 23, 2011. He was just 24 years old.But Sepang was also the place where Simoncelli achieved one of the biggest moments of his racing career. He won the 250cc world championship in 2008 at the same circuit.The Italian made his MotoGP debut in 2010 with Gresini Honda after becoming the 250cc world champion. His aggressive riding style and lively personality quickly made him a popular figure among fans. He continued with Gresini in 2011 and secured his first MotoGP podium at the Czech Grand Prix. He added another podium at the Australian Grand Prix.However, his promising career came to a tragic end during the second lap of the 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix.MotoGP family keeps Marco Simoncelli's memories aliveMarco Simoncelli's father, Paolo, later founded the SIC58 Squadra Corse team in memory of his son. The team continues to carry his legacy forward. The MotoGP paddock has also made sure that Simoncelli is never forgotten. Riders regularly visit the plaque at the Sepang circuit, where the accident happened, to pay their respects. In 2012, the Misano World Circuit was renamed in his honour. The circuit is close to Coriano, his hometown on Italy's Adriatic coast.Simoncelli was lovingly known as 'SuperSic'. The nickname also became a reminder of his connection with Sepang International Circuit, with SIC being part of its name.Earlier this year, Gresini Racing also paid tribute to him at the San Marino Grand Prix. The team ran a special San Carlo-inspired livery as part of its 30th anniversary celebrations.Marco Simoncelliâs career that promised so muchMarco Simoncelli had already made a strong mark in motorcycle racing before his death. He won the 2008 250cc world championship with Gilera and finished third in the category in 2009.In MotoGP, he made 34 starts between 2010 and 2011, scoring two podium finishes and two pole positions. He was sixth in the 2011 championship with 139 points. His career statistics tell the story of a talented rider. But for those who loved him, the numbers will never be as important as the memories he left behind.Fifteen years later, the message from his parents says it all: Marco Simoncelli is still remembered, still missed and, above all, still loved.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
